title: Correctness of AND-normal-form conversion
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ variables — a tree of literals combined by AND and OR gates — and let $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$ be an assignment to those variables. Converting $c$ into strictly alternating AND-normal form and evaluating the resulting normal-form AND circuit at $x$ yields the same Boolean value as evaluating $c$ directly at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: c is a Boolean circuit on n variables
x is an assignment from Fin n to Bool
equality of the two evaluations at that arbitrary x
replaced:
For every circuit $c$ and assignment $x$,
$(c.\mathrm{toNAnd}).\mathrm{eval}\,x = c.\mathrm{eval}\,x$.
